$comment: Merge-queue parity policy (.github/MERGE_QUEUE.md "Queue parity"). Checked by scripts/ci-workflow-topology.test.mjs via scripts/lib/queue-parity.mjs.

exemptions.reason: Installs the dependency workspace of the synthetic combined head; on a PR the head is the PR itself, so there is nothing separate to build.
Decides whether this exact merge_group entry is still current in the queue; queue membership does not exist before admission.
Selects lanes from the combined diff against current main; the PR selects its own lanes inside Source Validation.
Only proves anything on a main push; on merge_group it emits neutral outputs that later jobs gate on.
Aggregates the ci-fast lanes of the combined head; each lane is classified on its own below.
Writes the product-lane receipt for the combined head that main release readiness later reads.
Aggregates the combined-head leaves into the PR Ready context on merge_group; the PR has its own aggregate in Source Validation.
The queue runs the typecheck lane of scripts/ci-fast-lanes.mjs; the PR runs a hand-copied typecheck in Source Validation, so a lane-only failure first shows in the queue.
The queue runs the remaining ci-fast lanes (actionlint, incident contract, storybook, playwright guards); the PR runs only a hand-picked subset of them.
The profile admission browser proof runs only in the queue; no PR job runs the same Playwright spec.
Structural python lanes run only in the queue; no PR job runs the same lane commands.
Structural web lanes run only in the queue; no PR job runs the same lane commands.
Structural lane-runner tests run only in the queue; no PR job runs the same lane commands.
Blog-only qualification runs only in the queue; the PR has no blog content lane.
The queue runs all 14 web unit shards plus packages/ui; the PR runs only tests related to its diff. Moving the shards onto PRs costs hosted runner capacity and needs a founder decision.
The PR coverage job builds and runs the route JS budget and SEO certification, but the layout guard Playwright pass runs only in the queue.
The Ovie production build runs only in the queue; the PR runs Ovie tests but not its build.
The Ovie typecheck runs only in the queue; no PR job runs the same command.
The Storybook surface matrix and the extension, ingest, canary and mesh package checks run only in the queue.
Path-selected iOS unit and coverage run only in the queue; the PR runs only the portable iOS contract.
Path-selected Mac build and test run only in the queue; no PR job runs them.
Cross-product contract package tests run only in the queue; no PR job runs them.
Deterministic promptfoo evals run only in the queue; no PR job runs them.
The golden eval set runs only in the queue; no PR job runs it.
The homepage and marketing visual snapshot compare runs only in the queue; the baselines lane owns closing it.
Database certification on an isolated Neon branch runs only in the queue, path-gated on DB changes; the PR runs the static migration guard only.
The Lighthouse dashboard gate never runs on a PR (about 80 queue failures in 7 days); the Lighthouse lane owns closing it.
The Lighthouse onboarding gate never runs on a PR; the Lighthouse lane owns closing it.

prOnlyInputs.why: Re-measures each member diff against the PR size cap and its labels; the same cap is required on the PR head.
Re-reads the fork origin and approvals of each member; the same gate is required on the PR head.
PR Fleet Rules reads the PR body and labels (receipts, red-before-green); it runs on pull_request only.

prOnlyExemptions.reason: Mostly a combined-head check: 41 of its 42 queue failures from 2026-11-04 to 2026-11-11 were the combined-tree byte budget and holds are read at admission. Only the per-member size cap is PR-only; it leaves the queue once the PR side re-checks a removed big-pr label.
The ruleset requires a Fork PR Gate context on merge_group; it spends no API call and is decided from the size job reads. Dropping it needs a ruleset change.
